open_questions: Centroid inconclusive prevents confirming an off-target EB, but on-target is not required to reject given on-target stellar eclipse evidence; high-resolution imaging/spectroscopy not needed to overturn verdict.
dossier.public_summary: The dip shows a second deep eclipse as large as half the first, which a planet cannot produce, and its depth vanishes in later sectors and changes even within the same pipeline. A few anomalously deep transits carry most of the signal while others are missing, inconsistent with a planet. Together this favours a small-star/binary eclipse on the target over a planet.

reasons.why: Significant second eclipse ~60% as deep as primary at phase 0.3105, well above brightest noise and brightening, indicating a stellar companion rather than a planet. Hot Jupiter secondary would be much tinier.

Depth changes dramatically between sectors (57±53 ppm in sector 49 vs 871±73 ppm in sector 22). Different light-curve products give strongly different depths (SPOC 2-min 752±48 ppm p_constant 0.0318 vs TESS-SPOC 113±50 ppm p_constant 0.0032).
reasons.value: 9.433e-22 depth_change_pct 156 sector depths 871, 664, 57, 495 ppm chi2 101 dof 3

reasons.why: Even within the same pipeline depths are inconsistent, so variation is astrophysical / systematics, not just calibration. A planet should be steady within a source.

Individual transit depths are not consistent; a few deep events drive the signal while two predicted transits are essentially absent. Low SNR (14.54, 14.15) with few transits (5 refit) makes this untrustworthy.
reasons.value: p_consistent 8.588180101571396e-22 mean_depth_ppm 461 share_of_top_3 0.809 outliers 19 ppm (-5.8 sigma) vs 1066 ppm (5.2 sigma)

reasons.why: ML scorer ranks as highly unlike known planets; though size is Neptune-like and shape is flat (v_sigma -4.242), duration is ~56% longer than central and flat bottom alone does not outweigh the strong secondary, extreme depth scatter, and top-3 dominance.
reasons.value: planet_rank 0.07 size rp_rearth 2.108 duration ratio 1.562 (observed_h 5.996 vs central_h 3.838)
